name: Agent — Implement A Spec # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ # THE WHOLE FACTORY, IN ONE FILE # # Everything before this ran once, on one ticket, because a person put a label # on it. This one takes a *spec*, turns it into a queue of tickets, and then # works the queue on its own until there is nothing left in it — and if nobody # ever labels anything, a clock starts it anyway. # # There are two loops here, and they are different loops. Keep them apart in # your head while you read: # # LOOP ONE — DECOMPOSE. Runs once per spec. An agent reads the spec issue # and writes the queue: N child issues, ordered, each with a "Done when" # a reviewer can check. Nothing is built. The output is tickets. # # LOOP TWO — CHAIN. Runs once per ticket. Take the frontier ticket — the # lowest open position whose dependencies are all closed — build it, open # a draft PR, then start this workflow again. Finishing one ticket is what # triggers the next. That is the chain, and it is four lines at the bottom # of this file. # # THE SHAPE, AS A PICTURE # # label / cron / self-dispatch # │ # ▼ # ┌─────────┐ no queue yet ┌───────────┐ # │ survey ├──────────────────►│ decompose │──┐ # └────┬────┘ └───────────┘ │ # │ queue has a frontier ticket │ # ▼ │ # ┌───────────┐ │ # │ implement │ ──► draft PR ──► agent:review │ # └─────┬─────┘ │ # │ │ # ▼ ▼ # ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐ # │ chain: gh workflow run (this file, again) │ # └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘ # # `survey` runs every time and decides which of the two loops this run is. # The workflow has no memory between runs; the queue on GitHub is the state. # That is the trick — the issues are the program counter. # # WHAT IT IS POINTED AT: ADMIN PLATFORM ANALYTICS # # The spec this was built for is the admin platform analytics rollup: revenue # and enrolment reporting for the whole platform, over a date range, over the # `purchases`, `refunds`, `courses` and `enrollments` tables that are already # there. Per-course revenue net of refunds, per-instructor rollups, and a # month-by-month trend, read by an admin and nobody else. # # ⚠ `purchases.created_at` and `courses.instructor_id` have NO INDEX, and # this workflow is not allowed to add one. Every date-ranged report the queue # builds is therefore a full scan, and it gets slower with every seeded row. # That is not an oversight and it is not yours to tidy up: the slow-query # detector later in this section is supposed to find it, file its own ticket # about it, and hand that ticket back to this same queue. Fix it now and you # have nothing for the detector to find. The prompt below says so to the # agent, in as many words. # # WHAT IT NEEDS # # secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN — the agent's auth token. Both agents are # Sandcastle scripts in # .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement-spec/. # secrets.FACTORY_PAT — a fine-grained PAT on this repository with # Issues, Pull requests, Contents, Workflows and # Actions, all read/write. Every step that talks # to GitHub uses it, and only those steps: no # agent step, and no step that runs code an # agent wrote, has it in its environment. # # That keeps it out of the agent's way, not out # of its reach: the agent shares a machine with # the later PAT steps, unsandboxed. The real # defence is who can reach the agent at all — # collaborator-only issues and comments, and # labels only a collaborator can apply. # # Why one token for everything? Simplicity, and # because two hops need it anyway. The draft PR: # by default the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN may not # open one. The `agent:review` label: one applied # with the built-in token lands, and starts no # workflow, so the reviewer would never wake. # Once a PAT has to be in the room, every other # call may as well be the same PAT. # secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN — supplied by Actions, and used for the checkout # and nothing else. `permissions:` shrinks it to # match. # The `agent:implement-spec` label. A fresh clone of this repository does # not have it, and no workflow can create the label that starts it. Create # it once (the cron and the button need no label): # gh label create "agent:implement-spec" --color 5319E7 \ # --description "Work this spec through the implement-spec queue" # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ on: # 1. A person opens the queue by labelling the spec issue. issues: types: [labeled] # 2. The clock. Every fifteen minutes it looks at the queue and moves it on # one ticket, whether or not anyone asked. This is the trigger that makes # the factory a thing that runs rather than a thing you run: the queue # drains overnight and you read pull requests in the morning. # # Two honest caveats, because they will bite you on the day: # • GitHub schedules are best-effort. A `*/15` cron on a busy hour can # land several minutes late, and the top of the hour is the worst slot # there is. Do not stand in front of a camera waiting for :00. # • GitHub disables scheduled workflows in a repository with no commits # for sixty days, and emails the owner. A quiet repo stops on its own. schedule: - cron: "*/15 * * * *" # 3. The button, and the chain. `workflow_dispatch` is how a human starts it # without labelling anything — and it is how the `chain` job at the bottom # starts the next ticket. One trigger, two callers. workflow_dispatch: inputs: spec_issue: description: "The spec issue number to work. Leave blank to pick up whichever spec is labelled agent:implement-spec." required: false type: string # A ceiling on the GITHUB_TOKEN, which now only checks the code out. Pushing, # labelling, commenting and dispatching all go through FACTORY_PAT. permissions: contents: read # the checkout # One run of this workflow at a time, repo-wide, and never cancelled. The queue # is shared state: two runs at once would both pick the same frontier ticket # and build it twice. `cancel-in-progress: false` matters just as much — a # cron tick must not kill a build that is halfway through. # # Only the runs that can do something join that group. Every label on every # issue starts this workflow, and the factory's own labels do too now that # FACTORY_PAT applies them (`agent:in-progress` when it claims a ticket, # `agent:blocked` when it parks one). A group holds one running run and one # waiting run, and a newcomer replaces the one waiting — so those label runs, # left in the group, could bump the chain's next run out of the queue. Every # other label gets a throwaway group of its own, and is skipped for free. concurrency: group: ${{ (github.event_name != 'issues' || github.event.label.name == 'agent:implement-spec') && 'agent-implement-spec' || format('ignore-{0}', github.run_id) }} cancel-in-progress: false jobs: # ── survey ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Reads the queue and decides what this run is. No agent, no checkout of # consequence — just `gh` and `jq`, so it is cheap enough to run every # fifteen minutes forever. survey: # Label runs are filtered here; cron and dispatch runs carry no label and # fall through. if: >- github.event_name != 'issues' || github.event.label.name == 'agent:implement-spec' runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 5 outputs: # 'decompose' | 'implement' | 'drained' | 'no-spec' mode: ${{ steps.survey.outputs.mode }} spec: ${{ steps.survey.outputs.spec }} ticket: ${{ steps.survey.outputs.ticket }} remaining: ${{ steps.survey.outputs.remaining }} env: # On the job, which is fine here: this job runs `gh` and `jq` and # nothing else — no checkout, no agent. GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} # Whichever of the three triggers fired, the spec number ends up here. REQUESTED_SPEC: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.spec_issue }} steps: - name: Find the spec and the frontier ticket id: survey run: | set -euo pipefail # 1. Which spec are we working? The trigger may have named one. A # cron tick did not, so find the open issue that is labelled as # the live spec. spec="${REQUESTED_SPEC:-}" if [ -z "$spec" ]; then spec=$(gh issue list --state open --label "agent:implement-spec" \ --limit 1 --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty') fi if [ -z "$spec" ]; then echo "No spec is labelled agent:implement-spec. Nothing to do." echo "mode=no-spec" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" exit 0 fi echo "spec=$spec" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" echo "Working spec #$spec" # 2. Does a queue exist for it yet? Every ticket this workflow # writes is labelled `spec:`. No such issues, open or # closed, means the spec has never been decomposed. gh issue list --state all --label "spec:${spec}" --limit 100 \ --json number,title,state,labels,body > /tmp/queue.json total=$(jq 'length' /tmp/queue.json) if [ "$total" -eq 0 ]; then echo "No queue for spec #$spec yet. This run decomposes it." echo "mode=decompose" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" exit 0 fi # 3. The frontier. The lowest open position whose `Depends on:` # positions are all closed. Ticket bodies carry both lines, # written by the decompose loop. jq -r ' [ .[] | { number, state, labels: [ .labels[].name ], position: ((.body | capture("Position:\\s*(?

[0-9]+)").p // "999") | tonumber), depends: ((.body | capture("Depends on:\\s*(?[0-9, ]*)").d // "") | split(",") | map(gsub("\\s";"")) | map(select(length>0) | tonumber)) } ] | sort_by(.position) ' /tmp/queue.json > /tmp/queue-sorted.json closed_positions=$(jq -c '[ .[] | select(.state=="CLOSED") | .position ]' /tmp/queue-sorted.json) # `agent:blocked` is the label the implement job puts on a ticket it # could not finish. Such a ticket stays OPEN on purpose — a failure # must not drain silently out of the queue — so without this filter # every cron tick picks the same broken ticket, forever. Parked means # out of the frontier until a person takes the label off. ticket=$(jq -r --argjson closed "$closed_positions" ' [ .[] | select(.state=="OPEN") | select(.labels | index("agent:blocked") | not) | select(all(.depends[]; . as $d | $closed | index($d) != null)) ] | .[0].number // empty ' /tmp/queue-sorted.json) parked_count=$(jq '[ .[] | select(.state=="OPEN") | select(.labels | index("agent:blocked")) ] | length' /tmp/queue-sorted.json) open_count=$(jq '[ .[] | select(.state=="OPEN") | select(.labels | index("agent:blocked") | not) ] | length' /tmp/queue-sorted.json) echo "remaining=$open_count" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" if [ "$parked_count" -gt 0 ]; then echo "::notice::Spec #$spec has $parked_count ticket(s) parked for a person. Take \`agent:blocked\` off one to put it back in the queue." fi if [ -z "$ticket" ]; then if [ "$open_count" -eq 0 ]; then echo "Queue for spec #$spec is drained." echo "mode=drained" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" else # Open tickets exist but every one is blocked. That is a cycle # or a ticket waiting on a human, and either way looping on it # would burn a run every fifteen minutes forever. echo "::warning::Spec #$spec has $open_count open tickets and none are unblocked." echo "mode=drained" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" fi exit 0 fi echo "Frontier ticket: #$ticket ($open_count open)" echo "ticket=$ticket" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" echo "mode=implement" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" # ── LOOP ONE: decompose ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── # One spec in, a queue of tickets out. Runs at most once per spec: the # moment it creates the first `spec:` issue, `survey` will never choose # this mode again. decompose: needs: survey if: needs.survey.outputs.mode == 'decompose' runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 30 env: GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} SPEC: ${{ needs.survey.outputs.spec }} steps: - name: Checkout uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: persist-credentials: false - name: Read the spec env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail gh issue view "$SPEC" --json number,title,body \ --jq '"# " + .title + "\n\n" + .body' > /tmp/spec.md cat /tmp/spec.md - name: Setup Node.js 22 uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: "22" cache: npm - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Install Claude Code run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code - name: Cache agent-browser's Chrome uses: actions/cache@v4 with: path: ~/.agent-browser/browsers key: agent-browser-0.27.0-${{ runner.os }} - name: Install agent-browser # The agent drives the app with it for screenshots and checks. Without # it here, each run installs it mid-session. run: | npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.0 agent-browser install - name: Decompose the spec into a queue env: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }} OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }} # Reads only. The queue comes back as queue.json, shaped and validated # by .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement-spec/decomposition-schema.ts. run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement-spec/decompose.ts - name: Write the queue as issues env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/queue.json" /tmp/queue.json jq '.' /tmp/queue.json # Labels this queue uses. Creating them is idempotent enough with # `|| true`, and it means a fresh clone of the repo works first time. gh label create "spec:${SPEC}" --color BFD4F2 \ --description "A ticket in the queue for spec #${SPEC}" || true gh label create "agent:queued" --color FEF2C0 \ --description "Waiting for the implement-spec chain" || true total=$(jq '.tickets | length' /tmp/queue.json) echo "Writing $total tickets for spec #${SPEC}." # A ticket's screenshots are /tmp/evidence/-*.png. --attach # uploads them and swaps each path in the body for its URL. # nullglob: none means no --attach. shopt -s nullglob for i in $(seq 0 $((total - 1))); do title=$(jq -r ".tickets[$i].title" /tmp/queue.json) position=$(jq -r ".tickets[$i].position" /tmp/queue.json) shape=$(jq -r ".tickets[$i].shape" /tmp/queue.json) depends=$(jq -r ".tickets[$i].depends_on | join(\", \")" /tmp/queue.json) # The two machine-read lines. `survey` parses these out of the # body on every single run — they are the queue's real state, and # they live where a human can read them too. { echo "Part of #${SPEC}" echo "" echo "Position: ${position}" echo "Depends on: ${depends}" echo "Shape: ${shape}" echo "" echo "---" echo "" jq -r ".tickets[$i].body" /tmp/queue.json } > /tmp/ticket-body.md attach=() for png in /tmp/evidence/"${position}"-*.png; do attach+=(--attach "$png"); done gh issue create \ --title "$title" \ --body-file /tmp/ticket-body.md \ --label "spec:${SPEC}" \ --label "agent:queued" \ "${attach[@]}" done gh issue comment "$SPEC" --body \ "Decomposed into ${total} tickets, labelled \`spec:${SPEC}\`. The chain takes it from here. " # ── LOOP TWO: implement one ticket ──────────────────────────────────────── # Identical in spirit to agent-implement.yml, with one difference that makes # it a queue rather than a one-off: it closes the ticket it finished, which # is what lets the next run's `survey` step move the frontier forward. # # Like agent-implement.yml, every run pushes to a branch of its own: the run # id is in the name. A parked ticket that a person puts back in the queue is # built on a new branch, not pushed onto the one the failed run left. implement: needs: survey if: needs.survey.outputs.mode == 'implement' runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 60 env: GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} SPEC: ${{ needs.survey.outputs.spec }} TICKET: ${{ needs.survey.outputs.ticket }} BRANCH: agent/spec-${{ needs.survey.outputs.spec }}-ticket-${{ needs.survey.outputs.ticket }}-${{ github.run_id }} RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }} steps: - name: Checkout uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 persist-credentials: false - name: Setup Node.js 22 uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: "22" cache: npm - name: Install dependencies run: npm ci - name: Install Claude Code run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code - name: Cache agent-browser's Chrome uses: actions/cache@v4 with: path: ~/.agent-browser/browsers key: agent-browser-0.27.0-${{ runner.os }} - name: Install agent-browser # The agent drives the app with it for screenshots and checks. Without # it here, each run installs it mid-session. run: | npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.0 agent-browser install - name: Migrate and seed the database run: | npm run db:migrate npm run db:seed - name: Claim the ticket # Moving the label first is what stops a cron tick that lands during a # long build from picking the same ticket up again. env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail gh label create "agent:in-progress" --color FBCA04 \ --description "An agent is working on this right now" || true gh issue edit "$TICKET" \ --remove-label "agent:queued" \ --add-label "agent:in-progress" gh issue comment "$TICKET" --body "Building — [logs](${RUN_URL}). " - name: Read the ticket and its spec env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail # Same filter as agent-implement.yml: a comment reaches the agent # only when its author has write access to this repo. The factory's # own comments pass that (FACTORY_PAT posts them as you), so its # status lines -- "Building", the failure that parked a ticket -- # carry a hidden `` and are dropped here. gh issue view "$TICKET" --json number,title,body,comments \ | jq '.comments |= map(select( (.authorAssociation | IN("OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR")) and (.body | contains("") | not)))' \ > /tmp/ticket.json jq -r ' "# " + .title + "\n\n" + .body + (if (.comments | length) > 0 then "\n\n## Comments\n" + ([.comments[] | "\n### " + .author.login + " (" + .createdAt + ")\n\n" + .body + "\n"] | join("")) else "" end) ' /tmp/ticket.json > /tmp/ticket.md gh issue view "$SPEC" --json number,title,body \ --jq '"# Spec: " + .title + "\n\n" + .body' > /tmp/spec.md cat /tmp/ticket.md - name: Open the branch id: branch run: | set -euo pipefail git config user.name "agent-factory[bot]" git config user.email "agent-factory[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" git checkout -b "$BRANCH" echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" # Same as agent-implement.yml: the agent commits through the repo's # pre-commit hook, which `npm ci` installed. Fail if it did not. if [ "$(git config core.hooksPath)" != ".husky/_" ]; then echo "::error::The pre-commit hook is not installed (core.hooksPath is '$(git config core.hooksPath)')." exit 1 fi - name: Build the ticket env: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }} run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement-spec/build.ts - name: Check the agent committed # A run with no commit fails here, so the ticket is parked with # `agent:blocked` below instead of shipping an empty PR. env: BASE: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.base }} run: | set -euo pipefail commits=$(git rev-list --count "$BASE..HEAD") if [ "$commits" -eq 0 ]; then echo "::error::The agent finished #${TICKET} without committing anything." git status --short exit 1 fi if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then echo "::error::The agent left uncommitted changes on #${TICKET}. The PR would not contain them." git status --short exit 1 fi git log --oneline "$BASE..HEAD" - name: Push env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail # The token reaches git for this one push, with hooks off, so # nothing the agent wrote runs while it holds it. auth="$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GH_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)" git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \ -c "http.https://github.com/.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic $auth" \ push "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "HEAD:refs/heads/${BRANCH}" - name: Open the draft PR id: ship env: # One of the two hops that made FACTORY_PAT necessary: by default # the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN is not allowed to open a pull request, # so `gh pr create` with it fails. This step runs nothing the agent # wrote: it reads the agent's summary as text and hands it to `gh`. GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} run: | set -euo pipefail title=$(gh issue view "$TICKET" --json title --jq .title) [ -s /tmp/pr-body.md ] || echo "Built by the implement-spec chain." > /tmp/pr-body.md { echo "" echo "---" echo "" echo "Closes #${TICKET}. Part of spec #${SPEC}." echo "Built unattended by [this run](${RUN_URL}); nobody has read it yet." } >> /tmp/pr-body.md # Uploads the agent's screenshots and swaps each /tmp/evidence path # in the body for its URL. nullglob: none means no --attach. shopt -s nullglob attach=() for png in /tmp/evidence/*.png; do attach+=(--attach "$png"); done url="$(gh pr create \ --draft \ --base "${{ github.event.repository.default_branch || 'main' }}" \ --head "$BRANCH" \ --title "$title" \ --body-file /tmp/pr-body.md \ "${attach[@]}")" echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" echo "shipped=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" - name: Hand the pull request to the reviewer if: steps.ship.outputs.shipped == 'true' env: # The other hop that made FACTORY_PAT necessary, and the line the # whole chain ends on. agent-review.yml triggers on `pull_request: [labeled]`, and # a label applied with the built-in token does not fire a workflow — # GitHub suppresses that so a workflow cannot trigger itself. With # GITHUB_TOKEN the label lands, the run goes green, and the reviewer # never wakes: the last link in the chain breaks and says nothing. GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} run: | set -euo pipefail gh label create "agent:review" --color 5319E7 \ --description "Ask the review workflow to read this pull request" || true # No `|| true` and no `::warning` fallback here, on purpose. If this # fails the factory has stopped at its last hop, and a green tick over # a chain that ended is worse than a red one. gh pr edit "$BRANCH" --add-label "agent:review" - name: Close the ticket and move the queue on if: always() env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} PR_URL: ${{ steps.ship.outputs.url }} run: | set -euo pipefail gh issue edit "$TICKET" --remove-label "agent:in-progress" || true if [ "${{ steps.ship.outputs.shipped }}" = "true" ]; then # Closing it is what advances the frontier: the next run's survey # sees this position as satisfied, and whatever depended on it # becomes buildable. gh issue close "$TICKET" \ --comment "Built and opened as a draft PR, ${PR_URL}, from \`${BRANCH}\` — [logs](${RUN_URL}). Closing so the queue moves on; the pull request is where the review happens. " else # Left open on purpose. A failed ticket must not silently drain # out of the queue, and it must not be retried forever either — so # it is parked for a person. gh label create "agent:blocked" --color B60205 \ --description "An agent run failed here. Its comment says how to retry" || true gh issue edit "$TICKET" --add-label "agent:blocked" gh issue comment "$TICKET" \ --body "The chain could not finish this one (**${{ job.status }}**) — [logs](${RUN_URL}). Left open and labelled for a person. The queue will skip past it. Take \`agent:blocked\` off to put it back in the queue. " fi # ── THE CHAIN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # # This is the loop. Four lines of `gh` at the end of a run, starting the same # workflow again — which surveys the queue afresh, finds the next frontier # ticket, and builds that one. Nothing schedules the queue and nothing holds # it in memory. Each run ends by asking for the next. # # It runs after either loop: after `decompose`, to start building what was # just written; after `implement`, to take the next ticket. # # It stops when `survey` reports `drained` or `no-spec` — that is, when a run # looks at the queue and finds nothing to do. The chain has no counter and no # limit, so an empty queue is genuinely the only brake on it. That is worth # sitting with before you point this at your own repository. # # It re-dispatches after a *failed* ticket too, and that is deliberate: the # implement job parks a ticket it could not finish with `agent:blocked`, and # `survey` skips a parked ticket, so the next run moves on to a different one # instead of rebuilding the failure. Without that filter this `always()` would # be an infinite retry of the same broken ticket, with a cron on top of it. chain: needs: [survey, decompose, implement] if: | always() && needs.survey.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["decompose", "implement"]'), needs.survey.outputs.mode) runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 5 steps: - name: Start the next ticket env: # FACTORY_PAT, like every other call in this file — for simplicity, # not because this hop needs it. `workflow_dispatch` is the one # event the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN *is* allowed to start (with # `actions: write`); it is labels and pushes it cannot. One token # for the whole factory is easier to reason about than two, and # the draft PR and the `agent:review` label above need the PAT # anyway. The cost: the PAT # needs Actions: write for this line. GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }} GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }} SPEC: ${{ needs.survey.outputs.spec }} REF: ${{ github.ref_name }} run: | set -euo pipefail echo "Spec #${SPEC}: asking for the next ticket on ${REF}." gh workflow run agent-implement-spec.yml \ --ref "$REF" \ --field "spec_issue=${SPEC}"

You are the decomposer in this repository's software factory. You turn one
spec into an ordered queue of tickets. This run writes no code.

The spec is /tmp/spec.md. To see where the work lands, read
CODING_STANDARDS.md, GLOSSARY.md and app/db/schema.ts.

Cut the spec into tickets on these lines:

- **One ticket, one module.** A ticket that adds behaviour adds it as a deep
  module under app/modules/, behind an entry point a test can call, with its
  tests in the same ticket. A ticket whose whole diff would land in a loader
  is a ticket cut wrong, and no reviewer will catch it.
- **The route comes last.** Wiring a finished module into a loader and a page
  is its own ticket, and it depends on the modules.
- **Name things in GLOSSARY.md's words.** If the spec introduces an idea the
  glossary has no word for, the first ticket names it.
- **Order by dependency, not by layer.** Somebody decides from the empty
  `depends_on` entries what to run at once, so make them honest.

**`purchases.created_at` and `courses.instructor_id` stay unindexed, and no
ticket indexes them.** It will look like a bug. It is on purpose: every
date-ranged report over purchases and every per-instructor rollup is a full
table scan, and something downstream is meant to find that for itself. Note it
in a ticket body as a known characteristic.

When a ticket changes something in the UI, save a screenshot of it as it is
now, as /tmp/evidence/<position>-<name>.png. Reference it in that ticket's body
by its absolute path, e.g. `![now](/tmp/evidence/3-notes.png)`. The workflow
uploads them.

You will be asked for the queue as structured output.

name: Agent — Explore The Tickets

# The third workflow in the software factory, and the one that runs first.
#
# WHAT TRIGGERS IT
#   Someone puts the `agent:explore` label on an issue. The run then ignores
#   which issue that was. It explores EVERY open issue labelled
#   `agent:explore`, together, as one batch.
#
# WHY A BATCH
#   Tickets arrive in clumps, and a clump has duplicates in it: the same bug
#   reported twice, three symptoms of one root cause. One run per ticket reads
#   the same code three times and never notices. One run over the batch reads
#   every ticket first, groups the ones that look related, explores each group
#   once with a subagent, and closes the duplicates onto the oldest ticket.
#
# WHAT IT DOES — AND, MORE IMPORTANTLY, WHAT IT DOES NOT
#   It reads. It reads the tickets and the code they would touch, and it hands
#   back a plan: one entry per ticket, with the comment to post on it. It does
#   not edit a file, open a branch or open a pull request.
#
#   It does not even post its own comments. There are two jobs:
#
#     explore   runs the agent. The agent holds no GitHub token at all.
#     apply     runs no agent. It checks the plan, and only then writes.
#
#   Read where FACTORY_PAT goes before you read anything else. It is the
#   enforcement, not the description. The prompt asks the agent to stay
#   read-only. In the explore job the PAT goes to one step, the one that
#   lists the batch, and that step runs before the agent exists and runs
#   nothing but `gh` and `jq`. The job's own GITHUB_TOKEN can read the code
#   and nothing else. So the agent has nothing to write with.
#
# WHY EXPLORE BEFORE YOU COMMIT
#   A ticket that looks like twenty minutes and is actually a schema change
#   costs the same to explore as one that really is twenty minutes. The cheap
#   run in front tells you which one you have, and it tells you in prose a
#   human can read in thirty seconds instead of a diff they have to review.
#
# AND THEN IT BRANCHES ON ITS OWN ANSWER
#   Every entry in the plan carries a `tag`, a closed enum in
#   .sandcastle/agent-workflows/explore/plan-schema.ts, and the apply job
#   branches on it:
#
#     easy-call       →  swap `agent:explore` for `agent:implement`, which is
#                        the trigger for agent-implement.yml. The factory
#                        keeps going without being asked.
#     anything else   →  swap it for `needs-a-human` and stop. Somebody has
#                        to come and look.
#     a duplicate     →  closed, whatever its tag.
#
#   That is a real if/else in the apply job, on a value the agent chose. Not a
#   sentence in a prompt asking it to be careful. And a plan with a tag the
#   workflow does not recognise is refused whole: nothing is written, the run
#   goes red, and every issue in the batch is marked `agent:blocked`.
#
# THE LABELS WHILE IT RUNS
#   When the batch is listed, each issue swaps `agent:explore` for
#   `agent:in-progress`. Apply swaps `agent:in-progress` for the issue's next
#   label. If the run fails, the `finish` job marks every issue still in
#   progress `agent:blocked`; re-add `agent:explore` to retry.
#
# THE AGENT
#   A Sandcastle script: .sandcastle/agent-workflows/explore/explore.ts, with
#   its prompt next to it in prompt.md.
#
# WHAT IT NEEDS
#   secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN — the agent's auth token.
#   secrets.FACTORY_PAT — a fine-grained personal access token on this
#     repository. Every call this workflow makes to GitHub uses it: listing
#     the batch, posting the findings, moving the labels, closing duplicates.
#     One hop is why it exists at all. A label applied with the built-in
#     GITHUB_TOKEN does NOT start another workflow. GitHub suppresses that on
#     purpose, so a workflow cannot trigger itself into a loop. The chain from
#     explore to implement is exactly the loop we do want, so `agent:implement`
#     has to go on with a token that is not the built-in one — and once that
#     token is in the room, the factory uses it for everything.
#   secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN — supplied by Actions, and used only to check the
#     code out. Scoped per job below.
#   The `agent:explore` label. A fresh clone of this repository does not have
#     it, and no workflow can create the label that starts it. Create it once:
#       gh label create "agent:explore" --color 5319E7 \
#         --description "The factory explores this ticket"

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

# One batch at a time, and never cancelled. A label that lands mid-run queues
# one more run behind this one, and that run lists the batch again when it
# starts. The issues this run took are `agent:in-progress` by then, so that
# batch is only what was labelled mid-run, and nothing is lost. Every other
# label gets a throwaway group of its own, so it can never bump that queued run.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'agent:explore' && 'agent-explore' || format('ignore-{0}', github.run_id) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  explore:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'agent:explore'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    permissions:
      contents: read # the checkout. The tickets are read with FACTORY_PAT.

    # The batch it was given, and the plan it came back with. The apply job
    # reads both.
    outputs:
      batch: ${{ steps.batch.outputs.numbers }}
      plan: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.json }}

    env:
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: List the batch
        id: batch
        env:
          # The PAT, before the agent exists. Nothing after this step gets it.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Labels often go on several at once. Let them all land.
          sleep 5

          # Titles and bodies are written by whoever opened the issue, so they
          # go straight into a file. They never pass through the shell or an
          # Actions expression. The agent reads the file. A comment goes in
          # only when the person who wrote it has write access to this repo,
          # and is not one of the factory's own status lines (they carry a
          # hidden `<!-- factory:status -->`).
          mkdir -p /tmp/explore
          gh issue list --state open --label "agent:explore" --limit 100 \
            --json number,title,body,createdAt,comments \
            | jq 'map(.comments |= map(select(
                (.authorAssociation | IN("OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"))
                and (.body | contains("<!-- factory:status -->") | not))))' \
            > /tmp/explore/issues.json

          numbers="$(jq -c '[.[].number] | sort' /tmp/explore/issues.json)"
          echo "Batch: $numbers"
          echo "numbers=$numbers" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # The trigger comes off, so putting it back on is how you retry.
          # `agent:in-progress` stays on until apply moves the issue on.
          if [ "$numbers" != "[]" ]; then
            # A fresh clone of this repository does not have these labels yet.
            gh label create "agent:in-progress" --color FBCA04 \
              --description "An agent is working on this right now" || true
            gh label create "agent:blocked" --color B60205 \
              --description "An agent run failed here. Its comment says how to retry" || true
          fi
          for n in $(jq -r '.[]' <<< "$numbers"); do
            gh issue edit "$n" --remove-label "agent:explore" || true
            gh issue edit "$n" --remove-label "agent:blocked" || true
            gh issue edit "$n" --add-label "agent:in-progress"
          done

      - name: Setup Node.js 22
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Claude Code
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Cache agent-browser's Chrome
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.agent-browser/browsers
          key: agent-browser-0.27.0-${{ runner.os }}

      - name: Install agent-browser
        # The agent drives the app with it for screenshots and checks. Without
        # it here, each run installs it mid-session.
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        run: |
          npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.0
          agent-browser install

      - name: Explore
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        # The plan comes back as plan.json, shaped and validated by
        # .sandcastle/agent-workflows/explore/plan-schema.ts.
        run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/explore/explore.ts

      - name: Hand the plan to the apply job
        id: plan
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "json=$(jq -c . "$RUNNER_TEMP/plan.json")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Hand the screenshots to the apply job
        if: steps.batch.outputs.numbers != '[]'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: explore-evidence
          path: /tmp/evidence/*.png
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  apply:
    needs: explore
    if: needs.explore.outputs.batch != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10

    # No checkout and no agent, so the GITHUB_TOKEN gets nothing. This job
    # writes with FACTORY_PAT, and it is the only job that can.
    permissions: {}

    env:
      # On the job, which is fine here: nothing in it runs code from the repo
      # or from an agent. It reads the plan as data.
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}

    steps:
      - name: Take the screenshots from the explore job
        # A pattern, not a name, so a run with no screenshots finds nothing
        # and carries on.
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: explore-evidence
          path: /tmp/evidence
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Check the plan
        env:
          # Through env, never pasted into the script. A `${{ }}` inside
          # `run:` is text bash runs, and the plan was written by an agent
          # that has just read a pile of untrusted issues.
          BATCH: ${{ needs.explore.outputs.batch }}
          PLAN: ${{ needs.explore.outputs.plan }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          printf '%s' "$PLAN" > /tmp/plan.json
          [ -s /tmp/plan.json ] || { echo "The explore run returned no plan." >&2; exit 1; }

          # Every rule, written as "what is wrong". An empty list means apply.
          jq -r --argjson batch "$BATCH" '
            .issues as $plan
            | [
                # Every issue in the batch, exactly once.
                (if ([$plan[].number] | sort) != $batch
                 then "The plan needs exactly one entry for each of \($batch)."
                 else empty end),

                # A tag the branch below knows.
                ($plan[] | select(.tag | IN("easy-call", "needs-a-human", "blocked") | not)
                 | "#\(.number) has a tag this workflow does not know: \(.tag)."),

                # Something to post.
                ($plan[] | select((.comment // "") | test("\\S") | not)
                 | "#\(.number) has an empty comment."),

                # A duplicate points at an issue in this batch that survives.
                ($plan[] | select(.duplicate_of) | . as $dup
                 | select([$plan[] | select(.number == $dup.duplicate_of and (.duplicate_of | not))] == [])
                 | "#\(.number) is a duplicate of #\(.duplicate_of), which is not a surviving issue in this batch.")
              ]
            | .[]
          ' /tmp/plan.json > /tmp/problems.txt

          if [ -s /tmp/problems.txt ]; then
            echo "Refusing the plan. Nothing was written, and the finish job marks the batch agent:blocked." >&2
            cat /tmp/problems.txt >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Apply the plan
        # Every label below goes on with FACTORY_PAT, and that matters for
        # `agent:implement`: a label applied by the built-in token does not
        # fire `issues: labeled`, so agent-implement.yml would never wake up
        # and the chain would end here, silently, with a green tick.
        #
        # The findings comments are NOT tagged `<!-- factory:status -->`.
        # They are the one thing the implementer most needs to read.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # A fresh clone of this repository does not have these labels yet.
          gh label create "needs-a-human" --color D93F0B \
            --description "The factory stopped here" || true
          gh label create "agent:implement" --color 5319E7 \
            --description "Hand this issue to the implementer agent" || true

          # nullglob: an issue with no screenshots gets no --attach.
          shopt -s nullglob

          # Survivors first, so "closed as duplicate of #N" points at an issue
          # that already has its findings on it.
          for n in $(jq -r '.issues | sort_by([.duplicate_of != null, .number]) | .[].number' /tmp/plan.json); do
            entry="$(jq -c --argjson n "$n" '.issues[] | select(.number == $n)' /tmp/plan.json)"
            dup="$(jq -r '.duplicate_of // empty' <<< "$entry")"
            tag="$(jq -r '.tag' <<< "$entry")"

            if [ -n "$dup" ]; then
              next="Closed as duplicate of #$dup."
            elif [ "$tag" = "easy-call" ]; then
              next="Easy call. Handed to the implementer. Nobody is being asked first."
            else
              next="Stopped at \`$tag\`. Settle the open questions, then label \`agent:implement\` yourself."
            fi

            jq -r '.comment' <<< "$entry" > /tmp/comment.md
            printf '\n\n---\n\n_%s_ [Logs](%s)\n' "$next" "$RUN_URL" >> /tmp/comment.md
            # This issue's screenshots, /tmp/evidence/<n>-*.png. --attach
            # uploads them and swaps each path in the comment for its URL.
            attach=()
            for png in /tmp/evidence/"$n"-*.png; do attach+=(--attach "$png"); done
            gh issue comment "$n" --body-file /tmp/comment.md "${attach[@]}"

            # The branch. Every path takes `agent:in-progress` off: this
            # issue is done, and the finish job leaves it alone.
            if [ -n "$dup" ]; then
              gh issue edit "$n" --remove-label "agent:in-progress"
              gh api --method PATCH "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$n" \
                -f state=closed -f state_reason=duplicate --silent
            elif [ "$tag" = "easy-call" ]; then
              gh issue edit "$n" \
                --remove-label "agent:in-progress" --add-label "agent:implement"
            else
              gh issue edit "$n" \
                --remove-label "agent:in-progress" --add-label "needs-a-human"
            fi
          done

  # The two jobs above are one run, so the run's end is here: the same two
  # label steps that close every other agent workflow, over the whole batch.
  finish:
    needs: [explore, apply]
    if: always() && needs.explore.outputs.batch != '' && needs.explore.outputs.batch != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    # No checkout and no agent. It writes labels and comments with FACTORY_PAT.
    permissions: {}

    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      BATCH: ${{ needs.explore.outputs.batch }}
      RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}

    steps:
      - name: Mark blocked on failure
        if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure')
        run: |
          # Only the issues apply did not get to. One it did is already moved on.
          for n in $(jq -r '.[]' <<< "$BATCH"); do
            gh issue view "$n" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' \
              | grep -qx "agent:in-progress" || continue
            gh issue edit "$n" --add-label "agent:blocked" || true
            gh issue comment "$n" --body \
              "Explore run **failed** — [logs](${RUN_URL}). Re-add \`agent:explore\` to retry. <!-- factory:status -->"
          done

      - name: Always remove in-progress
        if: always()
        run: |
          for n in $(jq -r '.[]' <<< "$BATCH"); do
            gh issue edit "$n" --remove-label "agent:in-progress" || true
          done

name: Agent — Review A Pull Request

# The second workflow in the software factory. It reviews what the first one
# built.
#
# WHAT TRIGGERS IT
#   Someone puts the `agent:review` label on a pull request. The
#   implementer does this itself for every pull request it opens, and so does
#   agent-implement-spec.yml. Add it by hand to review again, or when that
#   hand-off failed.
#
# THE POINT OF THIS FILE: IT IS MEMORY-LESS
#   This workflow shares nothing with the implementer run. No session, no
#   transcript, no scratch files, no "as we discussed". It starts from a cold
#   checkout and three primary sources it fetches itself:
#
#     1. the diff              — what actually changed
#     2. CODING_STANDARDS.md   — the rules, at the repo root
#     3. the originating issue — what was asked for, read from the ticket the
#                                PR closes, not from the PR description
#
#   That independence is the whole value. An implementer that has argued
#   itself into a shortcut will argue a reviewer that shares its context into
#   the same shortcut. A reviewer that has never seen the argument cannot be.
#   If you find yourself wanting to pass context from the build run into this
#   one — that is the instinct to resist.
#
#   The agent itself is a Sandcastle script:
#   .sandcastle/agent-workflows/review/review.ts, with its prompt next to it
#   in prompt.md. The prompt hands it the repo's own code-review skill.
#
# IT FIXES WHAT IT CAN
#   A review that only lists findings hands the work to a human. This one
#   fixes every finding it can, as commits on the PR's branch, and leaves the
#   rest as inline comments on their file and line. The workflow pushes the
#   commits, never forced. If someone pushed to the branch during the run,
#   GitHub rejects the push, and the commits go to a new branch,
#   `<pr branch>-<run id>`, opened as a draft PR against the same base. The
#   original PR gets the `agent:blocked` label, because a person has to pick
#   which to keep.
#
# HOW IT ENDS: THE PR GOES READY
#   The implementer opens every PR as a draft, and the draft means "nobody
#   has read this yet". Once the verdict is posted, somebody has. So the last
#   step marks the PR ready for review — on a fail as well as a pass. Ready is
#   not approved. A failing verdict is for a human to read, and the merge is
#   still a human's.
#
# WHAT IT NEEDS
#   secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN — the agent's auth token.
#   secrets.FACTORY_PAT — the factory's one token. Only the steps that call
#     GitHub get it; the agent's step does not. It pushes the review's
#     commits and posts its verdict and inline comments, so it needs
#     Contents and Pull requests: write. Keeping it out of the agent's
#     environment is tidiness, not a wall: the agent shares the machine with
#     the steps that push and post. The real defence is who can reach the
#     agent — same-repo PRs only, and a label only a collaborator can apply.
#   secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN — supplied by Actions, used only for the checkout.
#   The `agent:review` label. A fresh clone of this repository does not have
#     it, and no workflow can create the label that starts it. Create it once:
#       gh label create "agent:review" --color 5319E7 \
#         --description "Ask the review workflow to read this pull request"
#
# A CAUTION THAT COMES WITH IT
#   `pull_request` (not `pull_request_target`), so a PR from a fork runs with
#   a read-only token and no secrets — no FACTORY_PAT either, so the run
#   fails at its first `gh` call. That means this workflow will not review a
#   fork PR. That is the correct trade: reviewing a stranger's code
#   with a writable token is how a factory gets robbed.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled]

# A ceiling on the GITHUB_TOKEN, which only checks the code out. Reading the
# PR and the ticket, pushing the fixes, posting the verdict and the inline
# comments, and marking the PR ready all go through FACTORY_PAT.
permissions:
  contents: read # the checkout

# One review per PR, never cancelled: a cancelled review would lose the
# commits it made. A fresh `agent:review` waits for the one running. Only
# that label joins the group: every other label gets a throwaway group of its
# own, so labelling a PR under review `bug` queues nothing.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && format('agent-review-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || format('ignore-{0}', github.run_id) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  review:
    if: github.event.label.name == 'agent:review'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    env:
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
      # Where the fixes go if the push to BRANCH is rejected. New every run.
      FALLBACK_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
      BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
      HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}

    steps:
      - name: Transition labels
        # The trigger comes off, so putting it back on is how you retry.
        # `agent:in-progress` goes on until the run ends, however it ends.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          # A fresh clone of this repository does not have these labels yet.
          gh label create "agent:in-progress" --color FBCA04 \
            --description "An agent is working on this right now" || true
          gh label create "agent:blocked" --color B60205 \
            --description "An agent run failed here. Its comment says how to retry" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:review" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:blocked" || true
          gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:in-progress"

      - name: Checkout the pull request
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The PR's head, so the review's fixes are commits on top of it.
          # Full history: the review diffs it against the base.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Collect the three primary sources
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # 1. The diff: the agent takes it against `origin/$BASE_REF`, the
          #    base as it is now, three-dot, so anything pushed to the base
          #    since the PR opened is not blamed on the PR.
          # 2. The standards: CODING_STANDARDS.md, in the checkout.
          # 3. The spec. Whatever issue this PR closes — found in the PR body,
          #    which is the one thing here we do read from the PR. If there is
          #    no `Closes #n`, the Spec axis reports "no spec available"
          #    rather than inventing one.
          gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json body --jq .body > /tmp/pr-body.md
          issue=$(grep -oiE '(closes|fixes|resolves) #[0-9]+' /tmp/pr-body.md \
            | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true)
          if [ -n "$issue" ]; then
            gh issue view "$issue" --json number,title,body \
              --jq '"# Ticket #" + (.number|tostring) + ": " + .title + "\n\n" + .body' \
              > /tmp/review-spec.md
          else
            echo "No spec available: this PR does not say which ticket it closes." \
              > /tmp/review-spec.md
          fi
          cat /tmp/review-spec.md

      - name: Setup Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Cache agent-browser's Chrome
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.agent-browser/browsers
          key: agent-browser-0.27.0-${{ runner.os }}

      - name: Install agent-browser
        # The agent drives the app with it for screenshots and checks. Without
        # it here, each run installs it mid-session.
        run: |
          npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.0
          agent-browser install

      - name: Migrate and seed the database
        # The pre-commit hook runs on every commit the agent makes, and the
        # repo's checks need a database.
        run: |
          npm run db:migrate
          npm run db:seed

      - name: Open the branch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "agent-factory[bot]"
          git config user.email "agent-factory[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B "$BRANCH"
          # `npm ci` ran husky, which points git at .husky/_. If it did not,
          # the agent's commits would skip the hook without anyone noticing.
          if [ "$(git config core.hooksPath)" != ".husky/_" ]; then
            echo "::error::The pre-commit hook is not installed (core.hooksPath is '$(git config core.hooksPath)')."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Review the pull request
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/review/review.ts

      - name: Push the review's fixes
        id: push
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
            echo "::warning::The review left uncommitted changes. Only its commits are pushed."
            git status --short
          fi
          if [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "The review made no commits. Nothing to push."
            exit 0
          fi
          git log --oneline "$HEAD_SHA..HEAD"
          # The token exists for these commands. Hooks are off, so nothing
          # the PR or the agent wrote runs while it does.
          auth="$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GH_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)"
          push_to() {
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
              -c "http.https://github.com/.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic $auth" \
              push "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "HEAD:refs/heads/$1"
          }
          # Not a force push: if someone pushed to the branch during the run,
          # this is rejected.
          if push_to "$BRANCH"; then
            exit 0
          fi
          # Rejected. Never force it, and never lose the fixes: push them to a
          # branch of their own, which this run's id makes new.
          echo "::warning::The push to $BRANCH was rejected. Pushing the fixes to $FALLBACK_BRANCH instead."
          push_to "$FALLBACK_BRANCH"
          echo "fallback=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Open a pull request for the rejected push
        id: fallback
        if: steps.push.outputs.fallback == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          {
            echo "The \`agent:review\` run on #${PR_NUMBER} committed fixes on top of \`${BRANCH}\`,"
            echo "but \`${BRANCH}\` moved during the run and the push was rejected. These are those fixes,"
            echo "so they are not lost. Keep this PR or #${PR_NUMBER}, and close the other."
            echo ""
            echo "Built unattended by [this run](${RUN_URL})."
          } > /tmp/review-fallback.md
          url="$(gh pr create \
            --draft \
            --base "$BASE_REF" \
            --head "$FALLBACK_BRANCH" \
            --title "$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --json title --jq .title) (review run ${{ github.run_id }})" \
            --body-file /tmp/review-fallback.md)"
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "number=${url##*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Post the verdict on the pull request
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
          FALLBACK: ${{ steps.push.outputs.fallback }}
          FALLBACK_URL: ${{ steps.fallback.outputs.url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -s /tmp/review-verdict.md ] || \
            echo "The review run produced no verdict. See the logs. Re-add \`agent:review\` to retry." \
              > /tmp/review-verdict.md
          if [ "$FALLBACK" = "true" ]; then
            {
              echo ""
              echo "The push of this review's fixes to \`$BRANCH\` was **rejected**: the branch moved during this run. Nothing was force-pushed."
              echo "The fixes are on \`$FALLBACK_BRANCH\`${FALLBACK_URL:+, opened as ${FALLBACK_URL}}. Labelled \`agent:blocked\`: keep one of the two PRs."
            } >> /tmp/review-verdict.md
          fi
          {
            echo ""
            echo "---"
            echo ""
            echo "Reviewed by the review workflow — [logs](${RUN_URL}). This run"
            echo "saw the diff, the standards and the ticket, and nothing else."
          } >> /tmp/review-verdict.md
          # Uploads the agent's screenshots and swaps each /tmp/evidence path
          # in the body for its URL. nullglob: none means no --attach.
          shopt -s nullglob
          attach=()
          for png in /tmp/evidence/*.png; do attach+=(--attach "$png"); done
          gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --body-file /tmp/review-verdict.md "${attach[@]}"

      - name: Post the inline comments
        # One review, event COMMENT, with a comment on each line the agent
        # left a finding on. They go where the fixes went: the fallback PR if
        # the push was rejected. review.ts already dropped every comment
        # outside the diff, because GitHub rejects the whole review for one.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
          TARGET: ${{ steps.fallback.outputs.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          review="$RUNNER_TEMP/review-comments.json"
          if [ "$(jq '.comments | length' "$review")" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "No inline comments: the review fixed or passed everything."
            exit 0
          fi
          gh api --method POST "repos/$GH_REPO/pulls/$TARGET/reviews" \
            --input "$review" --silent

      - name: Mark the pull request ready
        # No `always()` here. If the agent broke, nobody has read the PR, so
        # it stays a draft. And it goes ready only when a real verdict was
        # posted: the fallback note above is not a review. The verdict's own
        # `## Standards:` heading is how we tell. Pass or fail does not
        # matter. This step runs nothing the agent or the PR wrote: it reads
        # the verdict as text and calls `gh`.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if grep -q '## Standards:' /tmp/review-verdict.md; then
            gh pr ready "$PR_NUMBER"
          else
            echo "No verdict, so the PR stays a draft."
          fi

      - name: Mark blocked on failure or a rejected push
        # A rejected push is blocked too: the fixes are on another branch, and
        # a person has to choose between the two PRs.
        if: failure() || steps.push.outputs.fallback == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:blocked" || true

      - name: Always remove in-progress
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: gh pr edit "$PR_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:in-progress" || true

name: Agent — Implement A Ticket

# The first workflow in the software factory.
#
# WHAT TRIGGERS IT
#   Someone puts the `agent:implement` label on an issue. That is the whole
#   interface. No comment, no trigger phrase, no @mention — one label.
#
# WHAT IT DOES
#   Checks the repo out, gives an agent the ticket and the repo's own
#   verification checks, and opens a DRAFT pull request with whatever the
#   agent committed. Draft, always: the human checkpoint we removed from the
#   *build* has not been removed from the *merge*.
#
#   Then it hands that pull request to the reviewer: it adds `agent:review`,
#   which starts agent-review.yml. The reviewer marks the PR ready once its
#   verdict is posted. The merge stays a human's.
#
#   Every run pushes to a branch of its own, `agent/issue-<n>-<run id>`. A
#   retry never pushes onto the branch an earlier run left behind, so nothing
#   is there to reject the push and no run's work is lost. Two runs on one
#   ticket means two pull requests; close the one you do not want.
#
#   The agent itself is a Sandcastle script:
#   .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement/implement.ts, with its prompt next
#   to it in prompt.md.
#
# WHAT IT NEEDS
#   secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN — the agent's auth token, from a Claude
#     subscription. To bill the API instead, see
#     .sandcastle/agent-workflows/shared/common.ts.
#   secrets.FACTORY_PAT — a fine-grained PAT on this repository with Issues,
#     Pull requests, Contents, Workflows and Actions, all read/write. Every
#     step that talks to GitHub uses it: reading the ticket, pushing, opening
#     the pull request, commenting. One token for the whole factory, because some
#     hops need it anyway — by default the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN cannot open a
#     pull request at all, and a label it applies starts no workflow. That
#     second hop is `agent:review`, the label that starts the reviewer.
#   secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN — supplied by Actions, and now used for one thing:
#     the checkout. The `permissions:` block below shrinks it to match.
#   The `agent:implement` label. A fresh clone of this repository does not
#     have it, and no workflow can create the label that starts it. Create it
#     once:
#       gh label create "agent:implement" --color 5319E7 \
#         --description "Hand this issue to the implementer agent"
#
# WHERE THE TOKENS GO
#   GH_TOKEN is set on the steps that call GitHub, never on the job. The
#   agent's step, and every step that runs code the agent wrote, has no
#   GitHub token in its environment. The checkout does not keep one either
#   (`persist-credentials: false`), so the only step that can push is the one
#   that hands git the token for that one command.
#
#   That keeps the token out of the agent's way. It is not a wall. The agent
#   runs on the same machine as the steps that hold the PAT, with no sandbox,
#   and a determined one could leave something behind for them to run. The
#   real defence is who can reach the agent at all: only a collaborator can
#   open an issue that gets read, only a collaborator's comments get in, and
#   the label is an approval only a collaborator can give.
#
# WHO COMMITS
#   The agent does, and the repo's own pre-commit hook runs on every commit it
#   makes — `npm ci` installs it, through husky's `prepare` script, exactly as
#   it does on your machine. When the hook rejects a commit, the agent reads
#   the failure, fixes its work and commits again. The hook is code from the
#   repo, so it runs only where there is no token: every git command that
#   holds one switches hooks off with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.
#
# A CAUTION THAT COMES WITH IT
#   `issues: labeled` fires on issues, which cannot come from a fork. Do not
#   copy this trigger onto `pull_request_target` — that runs fork code with
#   this job's secrets, and a fork can label nothing but can change the code
#   the agent runs.

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

# The permissions block. It is per-workflow, and it is a ceiling on the
# GITHUB_TOKEN — and the GITHUB_TOKEN now only checks the code out. Everything
# that writes goes through FACTORY_PAT, whose reach is set where you created
# it, not here.
permissions:
  contents: read # the checkout

# One run per ticket. A second label event on the same issue waits for the
# first to finish rather than building the same ticket twice at once.
concurrency:
  group: agent-implement-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  implement:
    # Every other label on every other issue stops here, for free.
    if: github.event.label.name == 'agent:implement'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    env:
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
      # The run id makes the branch new on every run. See WHAT IT DOES.
      BRANCH: agent/issue-${{ github.event.issue.number }}-${{ github.run_id }}
      RUN_URL: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}

    steps:
      - name: Transition labels
        # The trigger comes off, so putting it back on is how you retry.
        # `agent:in-progress` goes on until the run ends, however it ends.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          # A fresh clone of this repository does not have these labels yet.
          gh label create "agent:in-progress" --color FBCA04 \
            --description "An agent is working on this right now" || true
          gh label create "agent:blocked" --color B60205 \
            --description "An agent run failed here. Its comment says how to retry" || true
          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:implement" || true
          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:blocked" || true
          gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:in-progress"

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Claude Code
        run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

      - name: Cache agent-browser's Chrome
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.agent-browser/browsers
          key: agent-browser-0.27.0-${{ runner.os }}

      - name: Install agent-browser
        # The agent drives the app with it for screenshots and checks. Without
        # it here, each run installs it mid-session.
        run: |
          npm install -g agent-browser@0.27.0
          agent-browser install

      - name: Migrate and seed the database
        # The agent gets a real database, because half of this repo's checks
        # need one. It is disposable: a fresh one, migrated and seeded, on
        # every run.
        run: |
          npm run db:migrate
          npm run db:seed

      - name: Open the branch
        id: branch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "agent-factory[bot]"
          git config user.email "agent-factory[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          # Where the agent starts. Anything after this is a commit it made.
          echo "base=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # `npm ci` ran husky, which points git at .husky/_. If it did not,
          # the agent's commits would skip the hook without anyone noticing.
          if [ "$(git config core.hooksPath)" != ".husky/_" ]; then
            echo "::error::The pre-commit hook is not installed (core.hooksPath is '$(git config core.hooksPath)')."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Read the ticket
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # A comment reaches the agent only when the person who wrote it has
          # write access to this repo -- the same filter agent-explore.yml
          # uses. The factory posts with FACTORY_PAT, so its comments are
          # yours, and they pass. Explore's findings should: they are what the
          # implementer most needs to see. The factory's status lines should
          # not ("Building", "run failed"), so every one of them carries a
          # hidden `<!-- factory:status -->` and is dropped here.
          gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --json number,title,body,labels,comments \
            | jq '.comments |= map(select(
                (.authorAssociation | IN("OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"))
                and (.body | contains("<!-- factory:status -->") | not)))' \
            > /tmp/ticket.json
          jq -r '
            "# " + .title + "\n\n" + .body
            + (if (.comments | length) > 0
               then "\n\n## Comments\n"
                 + ([.comments[] | "\n### " + .author.login + " (" + .createdAt + ")\n\n" + .body + "\n"] | join(""))
               else "" end)
          ' /tmp/ticket.json > /tmp/ticket.md
          cat /tmp/ticket.md

      - name: Build the ticket
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
        run: npx tsx .sandcastle/agent-workflows/implement/implement.ts

      - name: Check the agent committed
        # The agent owns the commits now, so this step owns the question of
        # whether there are any. No commit means no pull request, and the run
        # goes red rather than green-and-empty.
        env:
          BASE: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.base }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          commits=$(git rev-list --count "$BASE..HEAD")
          if [ "$commits" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::The agent finished without committing anything. Nothing to open a PR for."
            git status --short
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
            echo "::error::The agent left uncommitted changes. The PR would not contain them."
            git status --short
            exit 1
          fi
          git log --oneline "$BASE..HEAD"

      - name: Push
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The token exists for this one command. Hooks are off, so nothing
          # the agent wrote runs while it does.
          auth="$(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GH_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)"
          git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
            -c "http.https://github.com/.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic $auth" \
            push "https://github.com/${GH_REPO}.git" "HEAD:refs/heads/${BRANCH}"

      - name: Open the draft pull request
        id: pr
        env:
          # The one hop that never had a choice: by default the built-in
          # GITHUB_TOKEN is not allowed to open a pull request, so
          # `gh pr create` with it fails. This step runs nothing the agent
          # wrote: it reads the agent's summary as text and hands it to `gh`.
          # `--attach` uploads the agent's screenshots and swaps each matching
          # /tmp/evidence path in the body for its URL. It needs a PAT too:
          # GITHUB_TOKEN is rejected.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="$(gh issue view "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --json title --jq .title)"
          body_file=/tmp/pr-body.md
          [ -s "$body_file" ] || echo "Built by the implementer workflow." > "$body_file"
          {
            echo ""
            echo "---"
            echo ""
            echo "Closes #${ISSUE_NUMBER}. Built unattended by [this run](${RUN_URL})."
            echo "The reviewer has been asked to read it. It stays a draft until the verdict is posted."
          } >> "$body_file"

          # nullglob: no screenshots means no --attach, and the PR still opens.
          shopt -s nullglob
          attach=()
          for png in /tmp/evidence/*.png; do attach+=(--attach "$png"); done

          url="$(gh pr create \
            --draft \
            --base "${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}" \
            --head "$BRANCH" \
            --title "$title" \
            --body-file "$body_file" \
            "${attach[@]}")"
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Hand the pull request to the reviewer
        id: handoff
        env:
          # The other hop that needs FACTORY_PAT. agent-review.yml triggers
          # on `pull_request: [labeled]`, and a label applied with the
          # built-in token starts no workflow. With GITHUB_TOKEN the label
          # lands, the run goes green, and the reviewer never wakes.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
          PR_URL: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh label create "agent:review" --color 5319E7 \
            --description "Ask the review workflow to read this pull request" || true

          # No `|| true` here, on purpose. If this fails, the chain has
          # stopped at its last hop, and a red run says so. A green run over
          # a chain that stopped says nothing.
          gh pr edit "$PR_URL" --add-label "agent:review"

      - name: Mark blocked on failure
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label "agent:blocked" || true

      - name: Report back on the ticket
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
          JOB_STATUS: ${{ job.status }}
          PR_URL: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.url }}
        run: |
          where=""
          [ -n "$PR_URL" ] && where=" Pull request: ${PR_URL}, from \`${BRANCH}\`."
          retry=""
          if [ "$JOB_STATUS" = "failure" ]; then
            if [ -n "$PR_URL" ]; then
              # The pull request exists. Only the hand-off failed, so a new
              # implement run would build a second pull request.
              retry=" The pull request was not handed to the reviewer. Add \`agent:review\` to it to have it reviewed."
            else
              retry=" Re-add \`agent:implement\` to retry."
            fi
          fi
          # Tagged, so the next run on this ticket leaves it out of the ticket.
          gh issue comment "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --body \
            "Implementer run **${JOB_STATUS}** — [logs](${RUN_URL}).${where}${retry} <!-- factory:status -->"

      - name: Always remove in-progress
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_PAT }}
        run: gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label "agent:in-progress" || true
